# Markdown-to-HTML Rendering Pipelines

Dimension: Server-side vs client-side markdown rendering, Mermaid diagram support,
code syntax highlighting, dark theme integration, and streaming performance.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Client-Side JavaScript Parsers

| Parser | Bundle Size | Speed (ops/sec) | CommonMark | Stars |
|--------|-------------|------------------|------------|-------|
| marked | 444 KB [33] | ~1,587 [33] | GFM | 36,636 [33] |
| markdown-it | 768 KB [33] | ~743 [33] | Yes [33] | 21,125 [33] |

marked is approximately 2x faster than markdown-it on README parsing [33]. markdown-it
provides CommonMark compliance and a plugin ecosystem for custom syntax extensions [33].

## Server-Side vs Client-Side: Decision Factors

| Factor | Server-Side | Client-Side |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Streaming compatibility | Must buffer complete blocks | Can render incrementally |
| Security (XSS) | Sanitize before delivery | Must sanitize rendered HTML |
| Dark theme | CSS classes (Pygments codehilite) | CSS classes or inline |
| SEO | Pre-rendered HTML | Irrelevant for localhost |
| Load distribution | Server CPU | Browser CPU |
| Mermaid support | Not practical (needs browser DOM) | Native |

For a localhost streaming app, **client-side rendering** is the stronger choice:

1. Markdown arrives incrementally via SSE -- client-side parsers can render on arrival
2. Mermaid diagrams require browser DOM for SVG generation [27][28]
3. SEO is irrelevant for localhost
4. Single-user app has no server load distribution concern

## Streaming Markdown Rendering

### The O(n^2) Problem [14]

Traditional markdown parsers re-parse the entire document on each new token. For a 20KB
response arriving in 100 chunks:

- Chunk 1: parse 200 chars
- Chunk 2: parse 400 chars (200 old + 200 new)
- Chunk 100: parse 20,000 chars
- Total: ~10 million character operations

### Incremental Solution [14]

Key insight: "Once a markdown block is complete, it will never change." After a paragraph
ends with a blank line, it is locked and unaffected by subsequent content.

Algorithm:
1. Detect stable boundaries (blank lines, heading markers, fence closings)
2. Cache completed blocks permanently
3. Only re-parse the actively-receiving pending block

Result: each character parsed at most once = O(n), approximately 10,000 operations for the
same 20KB document -- a **500x improvement** [14].

### Benchmark: Streaming Markdown Libraries [14]

Testing 38 actual markdown files (128.55 KB total):

| Library | Time (ms) | Relative |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Incremark | 519.4 | 1.0x |
| Streamdown | 3,190.3 | 6.1x slower |
| ant-design-x | 3,728.6 | 7.2x slower |
| markstream-vue | 14,683.9 | 28.3x slower |

Incremark supports marked (default) and micromark engines [14].

## Mermaid Diagram Integration

### Bundle Size Concern [27]

| Version | Size (minified) |
|---------|-----------------|
| v9.3.0 | 878 KB |
| v9.4.0 | 2.65 MB |
| v10.x | 2.69 MB |

The 3x increase from v9.3 to v9.4 was caused by Flowchart-elk and mindmap diagrams
introducing Elk and Cytoscape layout engines [27].

### Mitigation Strategies

1. **Lazy loading**: Detect mermaid code blocks in rendered HTML, load Mermaid only when
   needed [27]
2. **mermaid.tiny.min.js**: Lightweight CDN option introduced in v11.0.0-alpha.4 [27]
3. **ESM code splitting**: Only diagrams encountered during rendering are loaded [27]
4. **Web component approach**: beautiful-mermaid library provides a `<mermaid-diagram>`
   element; claims 100+ diagrams in under 500ms with SVG-only output and zero DOM
   dependencies [28]; CSS custom properties enable live theme switching [28]

## Code Syntax Highlighting

### Bundle Size and Performance [13]

| Highlighter | Core + Grammar (compressed) | Total (compressed) | Speed |
|-------------|-----------------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Prism.js | 5.0 + 4.6 KiB | 11.7 KiB | 0.5-0.7 ms |
| highlight.js | 8.9 + 4.6 KiB | 15.6 KiB | 1.1-1.4 ms |
| Shiki | 28.1 + 17.4 KiB | 279.8 KiB (incl. 231 KiB WASM) | 3.5-5.0 ms |

### Accuracy vs Size Trade-off [13]

- **Shiki**: Uses VS Code TextMate grammars; "understands all constructs and syntaxes
  without fail" [13]; supports all VS Code themes natively including dark themes; 7x slower
  and 18x larger than Prism
- **highlight.js**: Auto language detection; struggles with JSX attributes and uppercase
  function names [13]; middle ground on size and accuracy
- **Prism.js**: Fastest and smallest; fails on multiple base types in interfaces, nested
  types, type parameters [13]; Prism v2 appears abandoned [13]

### Recommendation

**highlight.js** balances accuracy, size, and ease of integration for a local app:

- 15.6 KiB compressed [13] is negligible for localhost
- Auto language detection reduces configuration
- Extensive theme ecosystem including dark themes
- Active maintenance (unlike Prism v2)

Shiki is superior for accuracy but the 279.8 KiB WASM dependency [13] (24x larger than
Prism, 18x larger than highlight.js) and 7x slower performance are unnecessary overhead
for a local tool. Prism's maintenance status [13] makes it a risk.

## Dark Theme Integration

All three highlighters support dark themes via CSS:

- **highlight.js**: Theme CSS files (e.g., `github-dark.css`, `atom-one-dark.css`)
- **Shiki**: CSS variables approach for light/dark switching
- **Prism.js**: Theme CSS files

For the overall app dark theme, the markdown renderer's output uses standard HTML elements
that can be styled with CSS. Client-side rendering with class-based output (rather than
inline styles) provides the most flexibility for dark theme integration.

## Gaps and Limitations

- No head-to-head benchmark of cmarkgfm vs mistune under controlled conditions with
  document-size breakdowns -- the "10-50x" figure from [11] is a range, not a precise
  measurement.
- Incremark [14] is a new library; production maturity is unverified.
- beautiful-mermaid [28] maturity is unverified (Jan 2026 blog post).
- No memory consumption data found for any parser.
- The interaction between streaming markdown rendering and Mermaid code blocks arriving
  in partial chunks is not addressed by any source.
- Pygments (server-side Python highlighter) was not benchmarked against client-side
  alternatives in any source with comparable methodology.
